decisions.reason: The button pull-up and active-LOW decision does not alter the independent display-backlight supply, switching, or PWM circuit.
The source explicitly distinguishes the PIR and touch inputs as unchanged pull-down circuits; their requirements are already established separately by the same message.
The candidate records connector placement and GPIO mapping on the separate main-board design; the integrated-board resistor-bias decision does not necessarily change those attributes.
Using the 3.3V rail for button pull-ups does not change the selected AXP2101 architecture, required rails, charging behavior, or efficiency goal.
VRTC and VBACKUP are addressed by a separate clause and existing same-message Event; the button-input modification does not alter the auxiliary-pin state.
Changing button resistor bias and connector-pin electrical behavior does not add, remove, or reclassify any connector in the main-board inventory.
The shared 3.3V reference is incidental; the button-input decision does not alter addressable-LED supply or logic handling.
The button pull-up configuration does not change the monitored rails, monitor IC, channel allocation, or stated current-coverage semantics.
The source does not place the button pull-ups on the switched-load circuit or change that circuit's topology.
Button pull-ups on the integrated board do not alter sensor-board logic compatibility or level-shifter requirements.
The source does not change standalone USB activation, LDO capacity, or the loads that must be powered in standalone mode.
Connecting input pull-ups to 3.3V does not change the DCDC1 3.4V configuration or its downstream 3.3V compensation target.
